plan.rationale: Initial plan with no prior feedback. Workload is tall-skinny: M=32, N=4096, K=4096, so only ceil(32/block_M) tile rows exist. Block domains include all allowed M/N/K tiles and stage/thread options to leave room for later exploration; swizzle is restricted to [0] to establish a conventional row-major baseline per instructions. Tiles must divide M,N,K: block_M in {16,32} divide 32, while 64/128 exceed M and divide it only as overshoot tiles; block_N and block_K given all divide 4096. Shared-memory estimate is max(2*block_K*(block_M+block_N)*num_stages, 4*block_M*block_N); with cap 32768 plus the hard portability cap, large block_M*block_N with multiple stages and/or block_K=128 will be limited, which is intentional to let the optimizer select feasible tuples. Weights are equal initially; because M has only 1-2 tile rows, reuse from swizzle cannot exceed 1-2 so traffic is dominated by 1/block_N, and launches are dominated by N/block_N. Next hypothesis after baseline: test changed thread or block_K domains, expanded N/stage choices, and swizzle>0 despite limited M to confirm whether the panel-reuse feature has any measurable effect; validate ranking against simulator traffic/latency and revise weights if locality gains do not materialize. Metal validates the exact source/config/TIR numerically but does not execute the CUDA binary; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements.

Attempt-00 baseline (block_M=32,block_N=64,block_K=32,stages=3,threads=256,swizzle=0) passed numerical/compile checks at 195.8 us simulated, using 18.4 KB smem and 50 regs. Since M=32 with block_M=32 there is exactly one tile row, so swizzle-based panel reuse (capped at ceil(M/block_M)=1) cannot help traffic; broaden block_N to include 256 to cut launches and 1/block_N traffic, and test block_K variants (32/64/128) since larger block_K may cut pipeline overhead but raises smem. Keep block_M in {16,32} (both divide M; 64/128 overshoot M and are dropped). Stages rise to {2,3,4} to test deeper pipelining given K=4096; stage=1 dropped since it loses pipeline overlap with no offsetting traffic benefit. Explicitly add a small non-zero swizzle domain [0,4,8] to test the panel-reuse hypothesis the instructions describe, acknowledging it should be neutral at M/block_M=1 for block_M=32 but may matter for block_M=16 (2 tile rows). Equal weights retained for now; next hypothesis after feedback: if traffic locality does not materialize (expected, given one tile row), re-weight toward pipeline and launches and consider changing the thread domain (e.g. drop 64 or keep 128/256) based on measured simulator latency. Scope note: Metal numerically validates exact source/TIR for the selected config; GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements, and CUDA binaries are not executed here.

Attempt-00 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3,thr=256,sw=0) gave 195.8us; attempt-01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=8) improved to 176.4us with lower regs (44). Both pass numerical/compile; GB10 values are simulator estimates, CUDA binary not executed. Since M=32, block_M in {16,32} only; 64/128 overshoot and divide poorly. Keep block_N/{64,128,256} and block_K/{32,64,128} to test larger K tiles and wider N. Stages {2,3,4} (drop 1, no overlap benefit). Keep threads {128,256} (drop 64, which produced no winner yet and reg pressure/layout is unpriced) to test the changed thread-domain hypothesis early. Now that M/block_M=1 or 2, add full swizzle domain [0,4,8,16,32,64] to check whether panel reuse ever materializes at this shape; the analytic reuse is min(swizzle,ceil(M/block_M))<=2, so gains are expected to be marginal, and if simulator traffic stays flat we will down-weight traffic in later rounds. Slightly raise launches weight to 1.5 because N/block_N dominates block count (and small M needs enough blocks); traffic kept at 1 pending observed locality, pipeline/footprint at 1 to penalize smem-heavy stage=4/block_K=128 tuples under the 32768 cap plus hard portability cap. Next hypothesis: test whether block_K=128 with fewer stages reduces simulated latency more than w=N=256; if the wider N tile loses due to launch/occupancy tradeoffs, revert to N in {64,128}.

History: attempt-00 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3,thr=256,sw=0) = 195.8us; attempt-01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=8) = 176.4us best; attempt-02 repeated the exact attempt-00 tuple (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3,thr=256,sw=64) and reproduced 195.8us, confirming swizzle=64 is inert at M/block_M=1 (reuse capped at 1). Since M=32, block_M in {16,32} only (64/128 overshoot). Drop block_K=32: it lost twice, and the best result used K=64 with N=64. Keep block_N {64,128,256} to test wider N once from a winning thread domain, and block_K {64,128} to probe whether a deeper K tile offsets the N=256 smem cost. Stages {2,3,4}; stage=4 still untested and is now prioritized per instructions. Threads {128,256}: 64 never won and register/warp layout is unpriced, so exclude it and test 128 as the changed thread domain. Launch weight 1.5 retained because N/block_N drives block count and M gives only 1-2 tile rows; traffic weight 1 retained though observed DRAM is identical across attempts (33.8 MB), which argues the reuse proxy is not yet delivering locality gains -- if the next winner keeps DRAM flat, down-weight traffic further. Footprint/pipeline at 1 to penalize stage=4 + K=128 + N=256 tuples under the 32768 cap plus hard portability cap. Next hypothesis: from the attempt-01 winning shape family, test threads=128 with block_K=128/stage>=3 (or N=128) to see if lower thread count and deeper K reduce simulator latency more than wider N=256. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but the CUDA binary is not executed, so compile/memory status here is scoped, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.

History: attempt-00 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3,thr=256,sw=0)=195.8us; attempt-01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=8)=176.4us; attempt-02 reproduced attempt-00 exactly with sw=64 (195.8us), confirming swizzle is inert at M/block_M=1; attempt-03 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=64)=147.7us best. Key observed signals: DRAM is identical (33.8 MB) across all attempts including swizzle variants, so the panel-reuse proxy has NOT produced measured traffic gains at this shape -- hence down-weight traffic to 0.3 so it stops steering selection toward swizzle/tile choices that do not pay off. DRAM flatness also means block_N=64 already saturates reuse; keep N in {64,128,256} so solver may test wider N once, but launches weight stays 1.5 to favor N=256/128 if block count matters. block_K=32 lost repeatedly and is dropped; keep {64,128} to probe deeper K (attempt-01 already showed K=64 helps vs K=32, and larger K cuts pipeline iterations at fixed stages). block_M {16,32} only (M=32; 64/128 overshoot and did not win). Stages {2,3,4}: stage=4 still untested and now prioritized; stage=2 currently wins, stage=3 won at thr=256 earlier, so keep both. Thread domain changed to [128] as the early changed-thread hypothesis: attempt-03 did not use thr=128, and 64 never won, so we isolate 128 against the 256 winners to see if lower thread count with unpriced warp layout helps. Swizzle domain kept full [0,4,8,16,32,64] but traffic weight low so it does not dominate; if another swizzle variant reproduces flat DRAM/latency, we will further cut swizzle. Pipeline/footprint weights at 1 to penalize smem-heavy stage=4+K=128+N=256 tuples under the 32768 cap and hard portability cap. Next hypothesis: with traffic de-emphasized, test whether threads=128 with block_K=128/stage>=3, or block_N=128/256, beats the 147.7us K=64/st=2/thr=256 winner. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but does not execute the CUDA binary, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.

History: attempts 00/02 (M=32,N=64,K=32,st=3) both ~195.8us; 01 (M=16,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256) 176.4us; 03 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr=256,sw=64) 147.68us best; 04 (same but thr=128) 147.67us, essentially tied. Signals: DRAM identical at 33.8 MB across swizzle variants, so panel-reuse proxy gives no measured locality at M/block_M<=2 -> keep traffic low (0.3). block_K=32 lost twice (dropped); K={64,128} retained since K=64 clearly helped. block_M={16,32} only (M=32; 64/128 overshoot and never won). Stages={2,3,4}: stage=4 still untested and now prioritized per instructions. Threads: 128 vs 256 tied at the best tuple, so both retained to test the changed-thread hypothesis against a wider-N/K=128/stage=4 tuple. Swizzle full domain kept but low traffic weight so it cannot dominate; if a swizzle variant again reproduces flat DRAM/latency we further cut it. shared_memory_limit stays 32768 (hard portability cap binds anyway); footprint weight 1 penalizes stage=4+K=128+N=256 under the cap. Next hypothesis: test block_K=128 with stage>=3 and/or block_N=128/256 against the 147.7us winner to see if deeper K/stages or wider N beats the current best; GB10 values are simulator estimates (not hardware), Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but CUDA binary is not executed; no global optimality claimed.

Best remains 147.67us from attempts 03/04 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2, thr 256/128, sw=64); attempt-05 with sw=32 failed SMT bounds so never ran. Observations: DRAM flat at 33.8 MB across all variants including swizzle changes, so panel-reuse proxy yields no measured locality at M/block_M<=2; traffic down-weighted to 0.3. block_K=32 lost twice and is dropped. block_M={16,32} only (M=32). block_N kept {64,128,256} to test whether wider N ever beats the N=64 winner. block_K kept {64,128} to probe deeper K. Stages {2,3,4}: stage=4 still untested and now explicitly prioritized. Threads {128,256} since they tied at the best tuple; keep both to test thread hypothesis against wider-N/K=128 variants. Swizzle full domain retained but low traffic weight so it cannot dominate selection; swizzle=32 caused an SMT-bound failure previously, so the solver may naturally avoid it. shared_memory_limit 32768 with hard portability cap; footprint weight 1 penalizes stage=4+K=128+N=256 under the 32 KB cap. Next hypothesis: from the 147.7us K=64/st=2 winner, test (a) block_K=128 with stages>=3, (b) block_N=128/256, and (c) stage=4 at N=64, to see if any beats the incumbent. GB10 numbers are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but does not execute the CUDA binary, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate rather than a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.

Seven attempts observed. Best 147.67us: M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2 with thr 128 or 256 (attempts 03/04). Block_K=32 lost twice (195.8us) so dropped. Attempts 02/05 show swizzle variants (64, and sw=32 SMT-infeasible) leave DRAM flat at 33.8 MB and never beat the incumbent: at M/block_M<=2 the serpentine panel reuse proxy yields no measured locality, so traffic weight lowered to 0.3. block_M in {16,32} only since 64/128 overshoot M=32. block_N {64,128,256} retained to test wider N once against N=64 winner; block_K {64,128} to probe deeper K; stages {2,3,4} with stage=4 still untested and prioritized; threads {128,256} tied so both kept. Key change this round: collapse swizzle to [0] because all non-zero swizzles reproduced identical latency/DRAM and attempt-05's sw=32 was SMT-infeasible; freeing the solver from swizzle noise lets it spend the single selection on the structural axes (K=128 vs N=128/256 vs stage=3/4). Next hypothesis: from the K=64/st=2/N=64/thr~256 winner, test block_K=128 with stages>=3 or block_N=128/256 to see if a wider/deeper tile beats 147.7us; if DRAM stays flat we further de-emphasize traffic. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/config/TIR numerically but the CUDA binary is not executed, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.

Best observed is 147.67us from attempts 03/04/06/07 (M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2,thr 128/256); attempt-06/07 reproductions with sw=16/0 stayed at 147.68us and DRAM flat at 33.8 MB, so nonzero swizzle adds nothing at M/block_M<=2 and is collapsed to [0] per instructions once locality is shown absent. block_K=32 lost twice (~195.8us) and is dropped. block_M stays {16,32} since M=32 and 64/128 overshoot. Key structural change this round: drop block_N=64 (the incumbent already used it and swizzle variants were the only repeats) and force block_N into {128,256} so the solver must test whether a wider N tile beats the incumbent; similarly require stages {3,4} to finally exercise deeper pipelining, while keeping block_K {64,128} to probe deeper K (K=64 already beat K=32; K=128 untested with stage>=3). Threads {128,256} both tied at the winner, so retain both. traffic weight 0.3 retained because DRAM is invariant; launches 1.5 because N/block_N dominates block count at M=32; pipeline raised to 1.2 to favor deeper stages now that they are forced; footprint 1 penalizes stage=4+K=128+N=256 tuples under the 32768 cap and hard portability cap. Next hypothesis: from the K=64/st=2/N=64 winner family, test whether block_N in {128,256} combined with block_K=128 and stage>=3 or stage=4 reduces GB10 simulated latency below 147.7us; if wider N/deeper stages lose, revert N to 64 in the next round while keeping the changed-thread/K hypothesis. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but does not execute the CUDA binary, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.

Attempt-08 was MIP-infeasible because forcing block_N in {128,256} with stages {3,4} and block_K {64,128} leaves no tuple under the hard 32768-byte portability cap and shared_memory_limit 32768 (e.g. N=128,K=64,stage=3 already needs 2*64*(32+128)*3=61440 bytes > cap). So I re-open block_N to include 64 and narrow num_stages to [4] to fit a deep-pipeline probe within budget: N=64,K=64,block_M=32,stage=4 estimates max(2*64*96*4=49152, 4*32*64=8192)=49152 > 32768, which still exceeds the cap, so a truly feasible stage=4 tuple requires block_M=16 and N=64 with K=64: 2*64*(16+64)*4=40960 > 32768 too; only K=64,N=64,block_M=16,stage=4 stays over budget as well. Given the estimator, stage=4 may be infeasible for all tuples under the hard cap, so attempting it confirms the budget boundary rather than yielding a winner. Best remains 147.67us at M=32,N=64,K=64,st=2 (attempts 03/04). DRAM stays flat at 33.8 MB across all swizzle/stage variants, so traffic stays de-weighted to 0.3; swizzle fixed at [0] since nonzero panels reproduced identical latency and sw=32 was SMT-infeasible. K=32 lost twice and is dropped; block_K {64,128} retained; block_N {64,128,256} retained so the solver can still pick the incumbent N=64 or test wider N once feasible. Threads {128,256} both tied at the winner. Next hypothesis: verify whether stage=4 is representable under the 32768 cap; if attempt-09 is again infeasible or reproduces the 147.7us incumbent, the next round should restore num_stages {2,3} and test block_K=128 with block_N=128 at stage=2/3, which is where an unexplored feasible deeper-K/thread tradeoff remains. Scope: Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality is claimed.

Attempts 08 and 09 were MIP-infeasible: forcing block_N>64 with stages {3,4} and block_K {64,128} exceeds the 32768-byte cap (e.g. N=128,K=64,stage=3 needs ~61440B), and stage=4 is infeasible for every block_M/block_N/block_K combo under the cap. So I revert to a feasible core: block_K fixed at [64] (won at 147.7us; K=32 lost twice, K=128 with N>=128 and stage>=3 is cap-infeasible), block_N in {64,128} (N=64 is incumbent; N=128 testable only at stage=2 with K=64: 2*64*(32+128)*2=40960B and max with 4*32*128=16384 gives 40960 > 32768, so only block_M=16,N=128,stage=2: 2*64*144*2=36864 > cap; thus N=128 also largely infeasible at K=64 stage>=2 — retaining it lets solver confirm), block_M {16,32}, num_stages {2,3} (stage=3 with block_M=16,N=64,K=64 gives 2*64*80*3=30720B<=32768, feasible and untested at the winner; stage=2 is incumbent). Threads {128,256} tied at 147.67us so both kept. Swizzle reopened to full domain per instructions even though prior nonzero swizzles (16,32,64) reproduced flat 33.8MB DRAM and identical ~147.68us latency at M/block_M<=1, so traffic weight stays low at 0.3; launches 1.5 since N/block_N dominates block count. Key hypothesis: the feasible unexplored structural point is block_M=16,N=64,K=64,stage=3 (feasible at 30720B) versus the incumbent block_M=32,N=64,K=64,stage=2; and smaller block_M=16 may change occupancy. Footprint weight 1 and pipeline 1 penalize cap-edge tuples. Scope: Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but CUDA binaries are not executed; GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; no global optimality claimed.

History: attempts 08/09 MIP-infeasible because stage>=3 with block_N>=128 and block_K>=64 exceeds the 32768-byte cap (e.g. N=128,K=64,st=3 estimate 61440B); stage=4 is cap-infeasible for every tuple. The incumbent 147.67us is block_M=32,block_N=64,block_K=64,st=2,thr 128/256 (attempts 03/04); many swizzle and thread reproductions (06/07/10) gave identical 33.8MB DRAM and ~147.68us, so the serpentine panel-reuse proxy shows no measured locality at M/block_M=1 and traffic stays low (0.3). Key structural change: force the one feasible untested point family, block_M=16 with block_N=64, block_K=64, num_stages=2 (estimate max(2*64*80*2=20480, 4*16*64=4096)=20480B, under cap). This tests whether halving block_M changes occupancy/epilogue overhead at M=32 (2 tile rows instead of 1) versus the incumbent single-tile-row shape; swizzle is fixed to [0] because every nonzero swizzle tested (8/16/32/64) reproduced flat DRAM and latency or was SMT-infeasible, and launches weight 1.5/n=64 keeps enough blocks to fill the machine. Threads {128,256} both tied at the winner, retained to resolve the thread domain cheaply. Footprint/pipeline at 1 to stay off the cap edge. Next hypothesis: if block_M=16/st=2 does not beat 147.67us, revert to block_M=32 and test block_K=128 only at block_N=64/st=2 if the estimate fits (2*128*96*2=49152B exceeds cap, so likely infeasible), otherwise accept the incumbent family and stop broadening. GB10 values are simulator estimates, not hardware measurements; Metal validates exact source/TIR numerically but the CUDA binary is not executed, so compile/memory status is a scoped estimate, not a hardware proof. No global optimality claimed.
